request.state:
TIDEMARK GROUP — PEOPLE OPERATIONS (UK)
Sabbatical application review: SAB-APP-2026-0219
Pack: (1) Sabbatical Leave Policy SAB-2 (issued 1 March 2024) with Amendment 2026/1; (2) Continuity of Service Guideline CSG-1 (extracts); (3) Career Break Policy CB-1 (extract, for comparison); (4) employee records; (5) application and manager's endorsement.

(1) SABBATICAL LEAVE POLICY SAB-2

1. Purpose
1.1 Sabbatical leave gives long-serving employees a period of paid leave for rest, study or voluntary work. It is granted once in any seven-year period.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Employer" — the Tidemark Group company that employs the employee on the date of application.
2.2 "Qualifying Service" — service counted in accordance with the Continuity of Service Guideline CSG-1, as at the day before the requested sabbatical start date.
2.3 "Year" — for the purposes of this policy, a period of 365 days of Qualifying Service. Qualifying Service is counted in calendar days.
2.4 "Grade" — the employee's grade in the Tidemark grading structure (E1 to E9).
2.5 "Performance rating" — the rating from the annual performance cycle (Outstanding, Strong, Meets, Partly meets, Does not meet).

3. Eligibility
3.1 An employee is eligible for sabbatical leave if, on the requested sabbatical start date:
  (a) the employee has at least five Years of Qualifying Service;
  (b) the employee's two most recent completed performance ratings are "Meets" or better;
  (c) the employee is not subject to a formal performance improvement plan or a live disciplinary warning; and
  (d) the employee has not taken a sabbatical in the previous seven years.
3.2 The application must be submitted at least three months before the requested start date.
3.3 The employee's line manager must endorse the application; the manager may propose a different start date for business reasons, but may not refuse an eligible application more than once.

4. Duration and pay
4.1 Sabbatical leave is four weeks on full pay, which may be combined with up to four weeks of annual leave.
4.2 During sabbatical leave, all contractual benefits continue.
4.3 Sabbatical pay is calculated on basic salary only; allowances for on-call or shift work are not included.

5. Return
5.1 An employee who resigns within six months of returning from sabbatical repays the sabbatical pay.
5.2 On return, the employee resumes the same role on the same terms.
5.3 An employee may be asked to share what they learned during a study sabbatical with their team.

6. Process
6.1 Applications are submitted through the HR portal (form SAB-A) with the requested start date, duration and purpose.
6.2 People Operations checks eligibility within 15 working days and informs the employee and manager of the outcome.
6.3 Where People Operations finds the employee not yet eligible, it states the earliest date on which the employee would become eligible, and the employee may re-apply for a start date on or after that date without further delay beyond 3.2.
6.4 Approved sabbaticals may be postponed once by the employee, by up to six months, without re-application.

7. Interaction with other leave
7.1 Sabbatical leave cannot be combined with unpaid leave or a career break under CB-1.
7.2 If the employee falls ill during sabbatical leave, the sabbatical is not extended.
7.3 Public holidays falling within sabbatical leave are part of the sabbatical.

8. Appeals
8.1 An employee may appeal against a refusal to the Head of People Operations within 10 working days. The appeal is decided on the policy as written; discretionary exceptions are not available.

AMENDMENT 2026/1 (approved by the Group People Committee, effective 1 January 2026)
A1 Section 3.1(a) is replaced by: "(a) the employee has at least five Years of Qualifying Service or, if the employee is in Grade E5 or above on the requested sabbatical start date, at least four Years of Qualifying Service;".
A2 Section 3.2: applications for start dates in December require four months' notice.
A3 The amendment applies to applications submitted on or after 1 January 2026.

(2) CONTINUITY OF SERVICE GUIDELINE CSG-1 — EXTRACTS
C1 Qualifying Service is continuous employment with the Employer, counted from the start date of the current period of employment.
C2 Transfers within the group: where an employee transfers from one Tidemark Group company to another without any break between the two employments, service with the previous company counts as service with the Employer.
C3 Re-hire: where a former employee is re-hired by the same company within six months after the end of the previous employment, the previous period of employment is added to Qualifying Service (the gap between the employments does not count). Re-hire by a different Tidemark Group company does not reinstate the previous period.
C4 Paid leave of any kind, including statutory maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave while paid, and sickness absence, counts as Qualifying Service.
C5 Unpaid leave: a single continuous period of unpaid leave of 90 days or fewer counts as Qualifying Service. A single continuous period of unpaid leave of more than 90 days does not break continuity, but the whole of that period is excluded from Qualifying Service.
C6 Secondments to external organisations with a right to return count as Qualifying Service.
C7 Periods on a zero-hours or casual contract with a group company before a permanent contract do not count.
C8 Periods of notice worked count; periods of garden leave count.
C9 Service with a company acquired by the group counts from the date of acquisition unless the acquisition agreement provides otherwise.
C10 Industrial action days: excluded but do not break continuity.
C11 Where an employee's contract is transferred by operation of law into a group company, service with the transferor counts.
C12 Calculation example (days): an employee who started on 1 July 2021 and has a single unpaid leave of 30 days has, on 30 June 2025, 1,461 days of employment, all of which count.

(3) CAREER BREAK POLICY CB-1 — EXTRACT (for comparison; not applicable to sabbatical leave)
CB 2.1 Employees with three years of service may take an unpaid career break of 3 to 24 months. For the purposes of CB-1, service is counted from the first date of employment with any Tidemark Group company, including earlier periods of employment if re-hired within 12 months.
CB 2.2 Career breaks do not count as service for any purpose.

    Grade: E4 until 30 September 2026; E5 from 1 October 2026 (promotion letter dated 12 August 2026).
    Leave history:

    Payroll absence export (codes: MAT-P paid maternity; UPL unpaid leave; SICK sickness; AL annual leave), 2024:

    Contract: permanent, full-time (37.5 h); location Bristol Harbourside office.

  Record B — Marta Rinaldi, employee no. TA-07712, Tidemark Analytics Ltd, Grade E6, continuous employment since 3 April 2018; sabbatical taken 2025.

(5) APPLICATION
Application SAB-APP-2026-0219 submitted 15 September 2026 by employee no. TA-10388: "Requested sabbatical: four weeks from Monday 1 February 2027, combined with two weeks of annual leave; purpose: completing a data-science certificate."
Line manager's endorsement (18 September 2026): "Fully support. Marta has been with Tidemark since 2021 and will be E5 by then."
E-mail from the employee to People Operations (16 September 2026): "For the service check — I first joined Tidemark in March 2021, so I'll have almost six years by February. I was away for a few months in 2022 but came back to the group."
Pension scheme record (Tidemark Group Pension Plan): pensionable service from 15 August 2022; contributions suspended 1 June – 22 November 2024.
People Operations checklist: notice ≥ 3 months ✓ (15 Sep → 1 Feb); ratings ✓; PIP/warnings ✓; previous sabbatical ✓; Qualifying Service ☐ (to be completed by reviewer).

(6) GROUP COMPANIES AND REORGANISATION NOTICE
Tidemark Group companies (UK): Tidemark Holdings plc; Tidemark Analytics Ltd; Tidemark Data Services Ltd (dissolved 30 June 2024 after the reorganisation); Tidemark Cloud Operations Ltd; Tidemark Insights Ltd (acquired 1 May 2023).
Reorganisation notice RN-2023-11 (issued 6 November 2023): "With effect from 1 January 2024 all employees of Tidemark Data Services Ltd transfer to Tidemark Analytics Ltd on their existing terms. Continuous service with Tidemark Data Services Ltd is preserved for all purposes. Employee numbers change from TDS- to TA-."
Recruitment file TDS-2231 (Tidemark Data Services Ltd, 2022): "External candidate (previously employed by Tidemark Analytics Ltd until 30.06.2022). Offer 28.07.2022, start 15.08.2022. Probation 6 months."

(7) GRADING STRUCTURE — EXTRACT
E1–E3: associate and analyst roles. E4: senior analyst / senior engineer. E5: lead / principal individual contributor, or team manager. E6–E7: senior manager, head of function. E8–E9: director and executive.
Promotions take effect on the date stated in the promotion letter. Grade changes are recorded in the HR system on their effective date.

(8) SUPERSEDED — SABBATICAL POLICY SAB-1 (1 January 2019 – 29 February 2024), EXTRACT
"S1.1 Eligibility: seven years' continuous service with any Tidemark Group company, counted from the first day of employment; breaks of up to 12 months are bridged. S1.2 Sabbatical: up to eight weeks, of which four weeks paid. S1.3 Unpaid leave counts as service."

(9) CORRESPONDENCE ON THE 2024 LEAVE
Letter from the line manager to the employee, 20 May 2024: "I'm happy to agree your request to extend your leave as unpaid parental leave from 1 June 2024, returning on Monday 25 November 2024. During this period you remain employed; your pension contributions and holiday accrual are suspended."
Letter from People Operations, 22 May 2024: "Your unpaid parental leave 1 June – 22 November 2024 has been recorded (code UPL). It does not break your continuous employment."

(10) SAB-2 FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (intranet, March 2024)
Q: Can I work for another employer during my sabbatical? A: No. Voluntary work for a registered charity is allowed.
Q: Can I split my sabbatical into two periods? A: No, sabbatical leave is taken as one continuous period.
Q: Does sickness absence count towards my service? A: Yes, see CSG-1 C4.
Q: I work part-time. Is my sabbatical shorter? A: No, it is four weeks; pay is at your contractual rate.
Q: Can my manager refuse? A: Only once, for business reasons, if you are eligible (3.3).
Q: When will I hear back? A: Within 15 working days of your application (6.2).
Q: Does a sabbatical affect my bonus? A: No; bonus eligibility is assessed under the Bonus Plan, and sabbatical leave counts as time worked for bonus pro-rating.
Q: Can I take a sabbatical immediately after returning from parental leave? A: Yes, if you are eligible; there is no minimum period back at work.
